MyTownView

Morton, Illinois issued 12 residential building permits in 2024, worth $5.5M. Single-family homes made up 100% of permits. We have 2 years of data from the Census Building Permits Survey. See also local economy and business directory.

Construction activity in Morton jumped in 2024, up 71.4% from the prior year with 12 housing units permitted. At $455K per unit, new builds are running 77% above the Tazewell County average of $257K, pointing to higher-end construction. Volume is still modest compared to neighboring towns (90% fewer units than the county average of 117), but the investment per project is strong. All permits were for single-family homes.

## Frequently Asked Questions

What types of building permits are tracked here?This page shows data from the Census Bureau's Building Permits Survey, which tracks permits for new residential construction (single-family homes, duplexes, 3-4 unit buildings, and 5+ unit buildings). It includes both the number of permits issued and the total construction valuation.

How do building permits indicate local growth?Building permit activity is a leading indicator of development and economic health. Rising permit counts suggest growing demand and investment in the community. A shift toward multi-family permits may indicate increasing housing density, while declining permits can signal an economic slowdown.

Where does this building permit data come from?Data comes from the U.S. Census Bureau's Building Permits Survey (BPS), which collects monthly reports from permit-issuing jurisdictions across the country. Annual totals are published for municipalities with populations over 1,000. Data is typically available within 6-12 months of the reporting period.
